title: Война порядков в квартире  (A War of House Rules in the Apartment)

segments.t: Welcome to Kukhnya Season 2, Episode 11. At the shared apartment, tensions flare between Nastya and Sasha as Sasha rearranges the kitchen and poisons the cockroaches without asking, causing Nastya to worry that the poison has made Pashka the turtle sluggish.
Слушай, хватит наводить тут в свои порядки.
Ты не переживай, я их уже потравила.
Я, конечно, знал, что черепахи медленные.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Thank you, Nastenka.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'thank you' and finishing on 'Nastenka'. Nastya answers right away.
'I did not find them.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'found'.
'By the way, that is a cool color.' Notice how Russian expresses 'by the way' and 'colour' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Wait, where is the trash can?' Nastya raises the pitch on 'trash bin' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Kostya answers right away.
'Right where it belongs.' In Russian, the idea of 'where' flows naturally into 'maybe' without extra filler words.
Слушай, хватит наводить тут в свои порядки.
'Listen, stop imposing your own rules around here.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'listen' before landing on 'rules'.
'You know what?' Notice how Russian expresses 'know' and 'what' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Nastya answers right away.
Ты не переживай, я их уже потравила.
'Do not worry, I already poisoned them.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'you' and 'not' in a few short words.
'And what about you.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'you'.
Я, конечно, знал, что черепахи медленные.
'Of course, I knew that turtles are slow.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'slow'. Kostya answers right away.
'I think our Pashka looks completely sluggish.' Notice how Russian expresses 'in my opinion' and 'sluggish' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Wait a second, Kostya.' Nastya anchors the line on 'to decide', while 'Kostya' completes the thought.
'Do not touch him.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'touch' to negate the statement. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Слушай, хватит наводить тут в свои порядки.
Ты не переживай, я их уже потравила.
Я, конечно, знал, что черепахи медленные.
When you watch Scene 1 of Episode 11, listen out for the exchange around a war of house rules in the apartment — you will recognize every Russian phrase right away. See you in the next scene.
